title: Enquirer’s Guide: What is Poisson’s spot?
summary: It is the bright point that ordinary diffraction can make at the center of a round obstacle’s shadow.
author: The Enquirer’s Guide Desk
paragraphs: This entry from The Enquirer’s Guide answers a question often put to the Society: “What is Poisson’s spot?”
It is the bright point that ordinary diffraction can make at the center of a round obstacle’s shadow.

Fresnel’s wave theory predicted it, and Arago observed it. Eideticians learned that particular apparatus can produce a further, distinguishable response there; the familiar bright point itself is an optical effect.

Readers should treat the answer as an introduction rather than a final authority. Eidetic science in Alderwick is reported through measurements, disputed interpretations and careful revisions, and a respectable enquiry may properly end with further questions.
